positive.prompt: Set up a local Frappe development site without installing bench or its system dependencies manually
Create an isolated Docker site to test a new ERPNext version without touching my existing bench
How do I start a fresh Frappe site using fm and add my custom app to it?
I need a throwaway Frappe site to reproduce a bug without polluting my dev environment

negative.prompt: Run bench migrate on my existing bench after adding a new app
Scaffold a new Frappe app with hooks.py and the correct module structure

evals.prompt: I want to spin up a local Frappe site with ERPNext installed using Frappe Manager. Walk me through creating the site, picking the right version, and getting the Desk accessible in the browser.
evals.expected_output: Step-by-step fm commands to create a site with ERPNext, configure the version, and open the site
expectations: Uses fm commands (fm create-site, fm shell, or equivalent) rather than classic bench new-site / bench get-app
Shows how to specify the Frappe/ERPNext branch or version in the fm command or config
Includes how to access the site URL after creation (default port or fm open)
Does not instruct the user to install MariaDB, Redis, or Node manually — these are managed by fm's Docker environment

evals.prompt: I have an existing Frappe Manager site running. How do I add my custom app from a local Git repository and install it on the site without rebuilding the whole environment?
evals.expected_output: fm commands to add the app source and install it on the running site
expectations: Uses fm app commands (fm add-app or equivalent) to register the local app path rather than hand-copying files
Shows how to install the app on the site with bench --site <site> install-app or the fm equivalent
Instructs running bench --site <site> migrate after installation to apply any new patches or schema changes
Does not suggest editing Docker Compose files directly as the first approach
